# A library struct only a test names reaches the test on every target. The Go
# targets drop each library struct the Model's source does not spell
# (golang.PruneStructDecls), and the test module is a file of its own, so a
# test building an `http.Response` did not compile: `undefined: Response`. A
# program's method on the imported type, `http.Response.fine`, reaches it too.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import http "sngl:http"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

func http.Response.fine(r http.Response) => r.status == 200

component page ui.node {
    ui.text("page")
}

func testATestBuildsALibraryStruct(t test.Test, c page) {
    var r = http.Response{status=200, headers={}, body=""}
    t.assert(r.fine())
}

ui.window {
    page()
}
